([[Montverde, Florida]]) | college = * [[Florida Gators men's basketball|Florida]] (2018–2020) * [[Gonzaga Bulldogs men's basketball|Gonzaga]] (2020–2022) | highlights = * First-team All-[[West Coast Conference|WCC]] (2022) * Second-team All-WCC (2021) * WCC Sixth Man of the Year (2021) * [[West Coast Conference Men's Basketball Tournament|WCC Tournament]] MOP ([[2022 West Coast Conference Men's Basketball Tournament|2022]]) * [[Southeastern Conference|SEC]] All-Freshman Team (2019) * [[Jordan Brand Classic]] (2018) * [[Nike Hoop Summit]] (2018) | medal_templates = {{MedalSport | Men's [[basketball]]}} {{MedalCountry|the {{bk|CAN}}}} {{MedalCompetition|[[FIBA Americas Under-18 Championship|FIBA Americas U18 Championship]]}} {{MedalSilver|[[2018 FIBA Under-18 Americas Championship|2018 Canada]]|[[Canada men's national under-18 basketball team|Team]]}} }} '''Andrew Nembhard''' (born January 16, 2000) is a Canadian [[basketball]] player. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Gonzaga Bulldogs men's basketball|Gonzaga Bulldogs]]. He previously played for the [[Florida Gators men's basketball|Florida Gators]]. ==College career== [[File:Andrew Nembhard (cropped).jpg|thumb|left|upright|Nembhard with [[Florida Gators men's basketball|Florida]] in 2020]] Nembhard was recruited to the [[University of Florida]] from [[Montverde Academy]] in [[Montverde, Florida]]. In his freshman season with the Gators, he started every game and tallied the fourth-highest freshman assist total in school history. After averaging 8.0 points, 2.9 rebounds and 5.4 assists, and finishing fifth in the [[Southeastern Conference]] (SEC) in assist-turnover ratio, Nembhard was named to the conference all-Freshman team.{{cite news |last1= Parler |first1= Denver |title=Nembhard Earns SEC All-Freshman Honors |url=https://floridagators.com/news/2019/3/12/mens-basketball-nembhard-earns-sec-all-freshman-honors.aspx?path=basketball-men |access-date=September 15, 2019 |work=[[Florida Gators]] |date=March 12, 2019}} Just a few days later, Nembhard hit a [[buzzer-beater]] to upset [[LSU Tigers basketball|Louisiana State University]] (LSU) in the [[2019 SEC Men's Basketball Tournament|2019 SEC Tournament]].{{cite news |last1= Caron |first1= Emily |title=Watch: Florida's Andrew Nemhbard Sinks Last-Second Shot to Upset LSU in SEC Tournament |url=https://www.si.com/college-basketball/2019/03/15/florida-andrew-nembhard-game-winning-shot-lsu-sec-tournament |access-date=September 15, 2019 |work=[[Sports Illustrated]] |date=March 15, 2019}} Nembhard declared for the [[2019 NBA draft]], but ultimately chose to return to the Gators for his sophomore season.{{cite news |last1= Thompson |first1= Edgar |title=UF freshman Andrew Nembhard declares for NBA draft |url=https://www.orlandosentinel.com/sports/florida-gators/os-sp-gators-basketball-news-20190413-story.html |access-date=September 15, 2019 |work=[[Orlando Sentinel]] |date=April 12, 2019}}{{cite news |title=Canadian guard Nembhard returning to Florida for sophomore season |url=https://www.tsn.ca/canadian-guard-nembhard-returning-to-florida-for-sophomore-season-1.1313576 |access-date=September 15, 2019 |work=[[The Sports Network]] |date=May 29, 2019}} As a sophomore, Nembhard averaged 11.2 points, 5.6 rebounds, and 3.0 assists per game and led the SEC with a 2.2 assist-to-turnover ratio.{{cite news |last1=Collings |first1=Buddy |title=Orlando area college basketball All Stars for 2019-20 |url=https://www.orlandosentinel.com/sports/highschool/boys-basketball/os-sp-hs-college-basketball-best-20200401-ua7uhgocpnhzpow3j52az7y2su-story.html |access-date=April 4, 2020 |work=[[Orlando Sentinel]] |date=April 3, 2020}} Following the season he declared for the [[2020 NBA draft]] but hired an NCAA-certified agent, allowing him the option to return to Florida.{{cite news |title=Florida guards Andrew Nembhard and Tre Mann declare for NBA draft |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/29101274/florida-guard-andrew-nembhard-declares-nba-draft-again |access-date=April 27, 2020 |work=[[ESPN]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=April 26, 2020}}{{cite news |title=Canadian guard Andrew Nembhard declares for NBA draft again |url=https://www.cbc.ca/sports/basketball/nba/andrew-nembhard-declares-nba-draft-again-canada-1.5545705 |access-date=28 April 2020 |agency=CBC |date=26 April 2020}} On May 30, 2020, Nembhard withdrew from the draft and entered the NCAA transfer portal.{{cite news |last1=Borzello |first1=Jeff |title=Sources: Andrew Nembhard to exit NBA draft, transfer from Florida |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/29245276/sources-andrew-nembhard-exit-nba-draft-transfer-florida |access-date=May 30, 2020 |work=[[ESPN]] |date=May 30, 2020}} On June 23, 2020, Nembhard announced that he would transfer to [[Gonzaga Bulldogs men's basketball|Gonzaga]]. He chose the Bulldogs over offers from [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke]], [[USC Trojans men's basketball|USC]], [[Memphis Tigers men's basketball|Memphis]], [[Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball|Georgetown]] and [[Stanford Cardinal men's basketball|Stanford]].{{cite web |last1=Conway |first1=Tyler |title=Florida Transfer Andrew Nembhard Commits to Gonzaga over Duke, More |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2897343-florida-transfer-andrew-nembhard-commits-to-gonzaga-over-duke-more |publisher=[[Bleacher Report]] |access-date=June 23, 2020 |date=June 23, 2020}} He was granted a waiver for immediate eligibility on November 24.{{cite news |last1=Borzello |first1=Jeff |title=Transfer Andrew Nembhard eligible to play for Gonzaga men's basketball |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/30382342/transfer-andrew-nembhard-eligible-play-gonzaga-bulldogs |access-date=November 25, 2020 |work=[[ESPN]] |date=November 24, 2020}} In his [[2020–21 Gonzaga Bulldogs men's basketball team|first Gonzaga season]], he primarily came off the bench (though he played more minutes per game than two Bulldogs starters), averaging 9.0 points, 2.4 rebounds, and 4.4 assists per game{{cite web|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/schools/gonzaga/2021.html |title=2020-21 Gonzaga Bulldogs Roster and Stats |website=Sports Reference CBB |accessdate=March 2, 2021}} for a team that entered its conference tournament unbeaten. Nembhard was named the [[West Coast Conference]]'s inaugural Sixth Man of the Year, and was also named to the all-conference second team.{{cite press release|url=https://wccsports.com/news/2021/3/2/wcc-unveils-2020-21-mens-basketball-all-conference-honors.aspx |title=WCC Unveils 2020-21 Men's Basketball All-Conference Honors |publisher=West Coast Conference |date=March 2, 2021 |accessdate=March 2, 2021}} As a senior, Nembhard was named to the First Team All-WCC.{{cite press release|url=https://wccsports.com/news/2022/3/2/mens-basketball-timme-tabbed-wcc-player-of-the-year.aspx|title=Timme Tabbed WCC Player Of The Year|publisher=[[West Coast Conference]] |date=March 2, 2022 |accessdate=March 2, 2022}} On April, 21, 2022, Nembhard declared for the [[2022 NBA draft]], forgoing his remaining college eligibility.{{Cite web |date=2022-04-21 |title=Zags' guard Nembhard to declare for NBA draft |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/33778131/gonzaga-bulldogs-senior-andrew-nembhard-declare-2022-nba-draft |access-date=2022-04-21 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}} ==National team career== Nembhard represented Canada in [[FIBA]] competition at the U-16, U-17 and U-18 levels.{{cite news |last1= McLamb |first1= Michael |title=Andrew Nembhard: Canada's latest great hope |url=https://usatodayhss.com/2018/andrew-nembhard-canada-fiba-americas |access-date=September 15, 2019 |work=[[USA Today]] |date=June 14, 2018}} In 2019, he made the senior national team for the [[2019 FIBA Basketball World Cup|2019 FIBA World Cup]].{{cite news |last1= Smith |first1= Doug |title=Aurora teen Andrew Nembhard just might be ready to take on the basketball world |url=https://www.thestar.com/sports/basketball/2019/08/09/aurora-teen-andrew-nembhard-just-might-be-ready-to-take-on-the-basketball-world.html |access-date=September 15, 2019 |work=[[Toronto Star]] |date=August 9, 2019}} ==Personal life== Nembhard is the son of Mary and Claude Nembhard. His younger brother [[Ryan Nembhard|Ryan]] plays basketball for [[Creighton Bluejays men's basketball|Creighton]].{{cite news |last1=Meehan |first1=Jim |title=Nembhard family has connections to Gonzaga and Creighton |url=https://www.spokesman.com/stories/2021/mar/27/nembhard-family-has-connections-to-gonzaga-and-cre/ |access-date=December 27, 2021 |work=[[The Spokesman-Review]] |date=March
